items.label: FIGURE 3.15
items.title: Amounts of primary energy and generation of electricity from fossil sources need to decline massively to reach net zero by 2050
items.content: The figure shows four stacked area charts representing 'a. Primary energy sources' for different income groups: High-income, Upper-middle-income, Lower-middle-income, and Low-income. Each chart plots Exajoules (y-axis) against time from 2020 to 2050 (x-axis). Legend: Fossil (dark blue), Nuclear (yellow), Renewables (red). Trends: In all income groups, the Fossil component (dark blue) shows a massive decline from 2020 to 2050, while the Renewables component (red) shows a significant increase to reach net zero targets. High-income: Fossil starts at approx. 200 Exajoules in 2020 and drops to approx. 25 Exajoules by 2050. Upper-middle-income: Fossil starts at approx. 250 Exajoules in 2020 and drops to approx. 50 Exajoules by 2050. Lower-middle-income: Fossil starts at approx. 100 Exajoules in 2020 and drops to approx. 25 Exajoules by 2050. Low-income: Fossil starts at approx. 3 Exajoules in 2020 and remains low, while Renewables grow significantly.
